statements.text: Mr. Lee, I want to begin with you, and I am wondering if you, briefly, could just say how does this bill on day one make the internet a safer place for consumers across the country?
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on the American Data Privacy and Protection Act discussion draft, during a Q&A exchange between Rep. McNerney and a witness.

statements.text: With growing examples of #OpenAI’s #ChatGPT presenting lies as fact, potentially constituting unfair & deceptive practices, the @FTC is taking steps to protect consumers and ensure AI is developed responsibly. Innovation is not an excuse to break the law.https://t.co/VgLDnmdvjW

Now they can have your son's voice. All it would take is maybe 3 seconds to develop that voice, and you absolutely think that you better act immediately or your child is in danger. [...] And so AI presents all kinds of challenges to us.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Jan Schakowsky at a House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on AI and data innovation.

statements.text: But I know that AI is one of those and you have been talking about that. What would you say is the biggest concern now of workers, actors, that really threatens your business and their livelihood?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI and data, questioning a witness about the actors' strike and AI's impact on workers.

statements.text:
Artificial intelligence has transformative potential but also has risks. AI is making fraud easier by letting scammers clone your voice.

The rise of AI proves that we need comprehensive federal data privacy legislation. Privacy is the foundation we must build on to regulate AI. https://t.co/T827KKPun6

Artificial intelligence, or AI, is transforming our lives from healthcare to Hollywood. The fuel for this innovation is consumers’ data. Consumers feel helpless online, and AI is only making it worse. Americans should have a say in how their data is used to create AI.
statements.venue: House E&C Innovation, Data, and Commerce Subcommittee hearing opening statement

statements.text: Scammers are running that old scam pretending to be your loved one but now are using AI to sound like them. A scammer needs as little as 3 seconds of your voice to clone it. [...] We must protect Americans from these dangers with comprehensive federal data privacy legislation. This must be the foundation we build upon to regulate AI.
statements.venue: House E&C Innovation, Data, and Commerce Subcommittee hearing opening statement

statements.text:
My bill restricts telemarketers from using an AI bot that sounds like a human without first telling you that it is AI, & it holds telemarketers accountable for using AI to break the law. 

The dangers of deceptive AI can't be overstated, we must implement pro-consumer guardrails.

As of late, AI has made matters even worse by deceiving people who think they are talking to another human, when in actuality, they are talking to a bot.

I just introduced a bill to curb AI robocalls. 

I'm proud to join @FrankPallone in the fight against intrusive robocalls.

America must be a leader in AI. However, Americans’ privacy cannot be sacrificed towards that goal. 

Data is the fuel for AI development and the everyday people who own that data must be in control of how it is used. #SOTU

AI is making it even easier to violate and abuse women and girls with nonconsensual deepfake pornography. And tech companies are profiting off survivors’ pain.

Enough is enough. Congress must act now!

Thank you to @RepAOC, @RepPressley, & @DemWomenCaucus for this crucial forum. https://t.co/BPt9D6xoho
statements.quoted:
DWC member @RepAOC & Policy Co-Chair @RepPressley led a conversation on the rise of nonconsensual, sexually explicit deepfake pornography & how to protect survivors with @SophiaBush & @OmnyMiranda of @SVPAOfficial.

Its a new era of gender-based violence & we are fighting back. https://t.co/QdAVlxLj8t

statements.text:
The dangers of deceptive AI and bogus claims can't be overstated. I thank the @FTC for cracking down on these bad actors who are defrauding consumers.
 
Congress must act to implement pro-consumer guardrails on this growing industry.
statements.quoted: FTC announces crackdown on deceptive AI claims and schemes: https://t.co/NVPbM8QY9F /1

statements.text:
AI developers should not misrepresent what their tech can do. 

If AI algorithms are not properly designed, they will only deepen existing inequality and further harm consumers.

We must continue to take action to implement common sense guardrails on this growing industry.
statements.quoted: FTC takes action against IntelliVision Technologies for deceptive claims about its facial recognition software: https://t.co/0RNd7llarJ

statements.text:
I'm also glad that companies will be required to minimize the data they are collecting and saving about kids.

This is crucial given the many data breaches that have occurred, on top of the growing use of kids’ data for AI.

Everyone, especially our kids, deserve safety online.

I am concerned about manufacturing jobs and when wondering how AI is going to fit into this, is there some reason to worry for everyday workers that their jobs will begin to disappear because of AI, a different way to get the technology out?
statements.context: Remarks by Rep. Jan Schakowsky during a hearing titled 'AI in Manufacturing: Securing American Leadership in Manufacturing and the Next Generation of Technologies.'

statements.text: So what it seems to me is now we are talking about AI, and you talk about risk. You used that word, ``risk.'' So do we have to go back further, or let's—we—if you want to just talk about risk with AI, what exactly are we talking about?
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on AI technology and American competitiveness.

statements.text: The Republicans’ 10-year ban on the enforcement of state laws protecting consumers from potential dangers of new artificial intelligence systems gives Big Tech free reign to take advantage of children and families. It is a giant gift to Big Tech and once again shows that Republicans care more about profits than people. This ban will allow AI companies to ignore consumer privacy protections, let deepfakes spread, and allow companies to profile and deceive consumers using AI.
statements.venue: House Energy & Commerce Democrats press release on AI state-law moratorium

statements.text: Last week Republicans voted to pass a 10-year ban on states regulating AI. This is a big handout to Big Tech. State laws protect consumers’ privacy, data, and help stop scams. We should be passing comprehensive federal legislation to protect consumers. The Republicans’ bill only takes away their rights leaving consumers unprotected online.
statements.context: Opening statement by the Subcommittee Ranking Member at a House Energy and Commerce hearing on AI regulation.

statements.text: And so I think it is absolutely something we should say, zero time—zero time—as we watch AI develop, not 10 years. We haven't done that for anything else. And for us to do that now makes absolutely no sense and puts all consumers at risk. And so I want to strongly be against this idea, which I think is reckless.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on AI regulation and U.S. leadership, where Ms. Schakowsky opposes a proposed moratorium on state or local AI regulation.

statements.text: And now, along comes AI. And my concern is that we have technology, but we also rely heavily on protecting consumers, which you mentioned yourself. And I am concerned that we are not getting what we need. And so I wanted to ask Ms. Kak. You talked a bit about some of the threats to consumers. What do you think are some of the most dangerous things and the most important things that we should regulate at this point when it comes to AI?
statements.context: Congressional hearing on AI regulation and U.S. leadership where Rep. Jan Schakowsky questions a witness.

statements.text:
There’s a reason attempts to block state AI protections keep failing in Congress: they’re unpopular, undemocratic, and dangerous.

Now the same Big Tech billionaires who stood behind Donald Trump at his inauguration are abusing executive power to get their way.

I’ve never backed down from a fight with powerful corporations, and I won’t start now.
statements.quoted: Breaking News: President Trump signed an executive order to neuter state laws placing limits on the A.I. industry. The order is likely to be challenged in court by states and consumer groups, experts said. https://t.co/R6F3nHmpaJ

statements.text:
Big Tech shouldn't get to write the rules for global AI.

That's why I joined @SenWarren in urging the Trump Administration to stand up for strong oversight of AI companies.

As AI becomes a bigger part of our daily lives, consumers deserve transparency, accountability, and strong protections. https://t.co/yyDEE6Sxvn

Under Chair Lina Khan, we worked hard to make “Made in America” a label consumers can trust.

As companies use AI to hide where products come from and spread false claims, the FTC must do its job: protect consumers and honest American businesses.
statements.quoted:
One of the areas we aggressively policed @FTC was Made in USA fraud. Labeling goods "Made in America" if they're actually imported is illegal.

Four months ago, President Trump also directed his FTC to police Made in USA fraud. But his enforcers are asleep at the wheel. 

Our team just uncovered that Amazon and Walmart are intentionally ignoring Made in USA fraud on their platforms and are even systematically using their AI chatbots to steer shoppers away from Made in America goods.

My colleagues @CntrLawEconomy tested their AI shopping assistants and found:
- they suppress results for "Made in USA" prompts while showing results for "Made in China" prompts
- they directly add  "Made in USA" labels even to goods that are clearly imported
- the AI agents admit that they have the capacity to flag fraudulently listed products but choose not to so they can protect foreign suppliers that make up a big chunk of revenue

Honest American businesses are paying the price.
